tools.label: Create a Shape Binder
tools.reason: ShapeBinder is multi-body plumbing: it imports a shape from another body/project. A single-body student tool has no second body to bind from.

tools.label: Create a Sub-Object(s) Shape Binder
tools.reason: SubShapeBinder is multi-body plumbing: it links part of another body or an external project into this one. A single-body student tool does not need cross-body links.

tools.label: Create a Clone
tools.reason: Clone is multi-body plumbing: it duplicates a whole other body for further PartDesign features. A single-body student tool repeats geometry with repeat()/repeatAround() instead.

Sweep a selected sketch along a path
tools.reason: The wasm OCCT build binds no pipe operation at all: zero of its exports match BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe or MakePipeShell (probed directly, and consistent with script-surface.ts extrudeHelix entry: no helix, no pipe ride). A pipe exists only on the BRIDGE side, where the real FreeCAD PartDesign::AdditivePipe is kernel-gated -- the studio button (SPEC-P1c) delivers it by mouse. A ModelDoc/Code-mode word would have nothing honest to lower into. STUDIO BUTTON NOW EXISTS (P1c-3, 2026-09-09): the earlier text claimed the studio button delivered this by mouse; it had never been built. It is built and kernel-gated now. MEASURED: a pipe needs its profile and path on DIFFERENT planes, and Rect/Circle Sketch only make XY sketches, so the button works only after drawing the path on a face (pick a face, then New Sketch). A coplanar attempt used to build nothing silently; the emitter now refuses and says so.

tools.label: Additive helix
tools.reason: The wasm OCCT build has no helix curve export and no pipe operation to ride one on (zero exports match /helix/i, BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe or MakePipeShell -- probed directly; script-surface.ts extrudeHelix entry records the same wall). The bridge side is exact (real PartDesign::AdditiveHelix/SubtractiveHelix, kernel-gated) and the studio buttons (SPEC-P1c) deliver it by mouse; a Code-mode word would be an approximation with nothing to ride. STUDIO BUTTON NOW EXISTS (P1c-3, 2026-09-09): the earlier text claimed the studio button delivered this by mouse; it had never been built. It is built and kernel-gated now. MEASURED: helix pitch (Height/Turns) must be >= the profile diameter or OCCT grinds rather than failing -- an offset profile at pitch 6.67 ran 14 minutes at 3.4GB in the container, and a 40mm Rect Sketch profile froze the browser tab. The emitter now checks pitch before building and refuses in ~50ms.

tools.label: Add an ellipsoid
tools.reason: A general ellipsoid (three unequal radii) is a sphere stretched unequally -- the one operation this wasm build cannot do: BRepBuilderAPI_GTransform is not bound and BRepBuilderAPI_Transform accepts only a uniform-scale gp_Trsf (measured in packages/script/src/script-surface.ts, the scale entry). The two-equal-radii case is already served: it is a revolve.

tools.label: Drill a hole in a selected sketch
tools.reason: hole() makes a simple through/depth hole only; counterbore, countersink, thread and standard sizes are queued (plan B3)

tools.label: Subtract an ellipsoid
tools.reason: Same wall as the additive ellipsoid: a general ellipsoid needs unequal-axis stretch (unbound BRepBuilderAPI_GTransform in this wasm build); the axisymmetric subtractive case is a groove.

tools.label: Create a multi-transform feature
tools.reason: A multi-transform stacks several patterns into one feature -- an expert compression of operations the student vocabulary already composes: linearPattern(linearPattern(x, ...), ...) says the same thing in words a beginner reads. No new word needed; the composition is the lesson.

tools.label: Create a scaled feature
tools.reason: Scaling IS the blocked operation: uniform scale is expressible as a primitive dimension, and the unequal-axis case hits the same unbound BRepBuilderAPI_GTransform the ellipsoids do (measured in script-surface.ts). A student resizes a dimension; PartDesign_Scaled is an expert modeling tool, not a beginner word.
